questions.q: Why does Kasparov say we should not fear computers taking our jobs?
a: History shows technology has improved life while human input stayed valuable
Machines will never be able to process large amounts of data
Governments will always ban computers from most workplaces
New technology has never changed the kind of work people do
questions.why: Lesson 1 points to the steam engine, electricity and computers as past examples of adaptation.

questions.q: What does Kasparov see as the core difference between human and artificial intelligence?
a: Humans experience emotions, while computers do not
Humans can calculate faster than any machine
Computers rely on intuition rather than data
Humans are unable to make strategic decisions
questions.why: Lesson 2 says emotion and psychological endurance are what separate people from machines.

questions.q: Why do even top chess players make many tactical mistakes?
a: Psychological pressure from their opponent affects their play
They have not memorized enough opening strategies
They are usually tired from long tournaments
They deliberately play weaker moves to confuse computers
questions.why: Lesson 2 attributes the errors to the emotional and psychological side of competition.

questions.q: What can computers still not do, according to lesson 3?
a: Invent entirely new questions beyond their original programming
Process more data than a human brain can handle
Play chess better than a grandmaster
Follow instructions written by their designers
questions.why: Lesson 3 says AI only asks questions based on the data humans initially built in.

questions.q: What does Kasparov say we should focus on instead of fearing job loss?
a: Adapting society to the new reality
Slowing down all research into artificial intelligence
Teaching machines to experience emotions
Keeping computers out of creative industries
questions.why: Lesson 1 ends by recommending adaptation rather than fear of automation.
